review_notes: Reviewed all 40 lines, the underlying cutoff, staircase, covector and planar-gradient definitions, relevant calculus lemmas, and callers. The planar-gradient identity appropriately uses the plane-specific API. The proposed generalization below was checked against source signatures but not executed in Lean.

findings.problem: This smoothness result unnecessarily requires a planar domain and infinitely differentiable inputs. Unlike the preceding gradient identity, its conclusion uses no planar structure. Its composition-and-arithmetic proof also works for inputs of any finite differentiability order.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalize the statement to:
 theorem contDiffOn_cutoff_shiftedStaircase
     {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
     {n : ℕ∞} {Ω : Set E} {u χ : E → ℝ}
     (hu : ContDiffOn ℝ n u Ω) (hχ : ContDiffOn ℝ n χ Ω)
     {h δ : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδh : δ < h / 4) (θ : ℝ) :
     ContDiffOn ℝ n (cutoffStaircase u χ (shiftedStaircase h δ θ)) Ω
First obtain ContDiff ℝ n (shiftedStaircase h δ θ) from contDiff_shiftedStaircase using ContDiff.of_le and the inequality (n : ℕ∞ω) ≤ ∞. Then use the existing add/mul/comp_contDiffOn/sub proof unchanged. Restricting n to ℕ∞ deliberately excludes the analytic order ω. No openness or UniqueDiffOn hypothesis is needed; empty Ω, n = 0, and trivial real normed spaces remain covered. Keep the staircase parameter inequalities unchanged.
findings.benefit: Users can apply the same cutoff construction to C¹ or Cᵏ coordinates and to real normed spaces of other dimensions, without reproving this closure calculation. Existing planar smooth applications remain special cases.

def cutoffStaircase {X : Type*} (u χ : X → ℝ) (P : ℝ → ℝ) (x : X) : ℝ :=
  u x + χ x * (P (u x) - u x)

theorem contDiff_cutoffStaircase {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {n : ℕ∞} {u χ : E → ℝ} {P : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hu : ContDiff ℝ n u) (hχ : ContDiff ℝ n χ) (hP : ContDiff ℝ n P) :
    ContDiff ℝ n (cutoffStaircase u χ P) :=
